content.thinking:
I'm tracing the timeline: the monthly-spend-feature flag went on at 13:37 and errors started immediately with a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py. It was reverted at 13:43 but then surprisingly flipped back on at 13:45, which is the puzzling part I need to dig into.

Looking at the logs more closely, even after the 13:43:18 revert, the flag kept evaluating as "on" through 13:44-13:45, with the error rate peaking at 41.5% at 13:44 — suggesting the revert didn't actually propagate to the service, possibly due to caching. Since the record explicitly states the mitigation was refuted, I'll trust that over my own interpretation of the logs.

So the M1 refutation doesn't actually disprove the flag as the cause—it just shows the revert failed to propagate to the service, which is still consistent with the flag being the root issue. I also note T21's check happened only a second after the revert, likely too soon to catch effect, and G971b shows the toggle actually occurred mid-minute at 13:37 (111 off, 89 on), with G7e5d confirming the flag was off for all evaluations from 13:07 to 13:36.

Now I'm piecing together the causal chain: baseline ClientDisconnected errors from G46bc existed before 13:37, but Gbac1 shows the error rate jumping from roughly 0.5-1.5% up to 41.5% right at the flag flip. The actual symptom is account page failures for shoppers, and G5309 pinpoints a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py starting exactly at 13:37 — distinct from the earlier ClientDisconnected errors, confirming this is a new failure mode tied to the flag change rather than a continuation of prior issues.

I'm checking the admin action (P1) that toggled the monthly-spend-feature flag on at 13:37, and comparing flag evaluation data before and after — G7e5d shows it was off for all requests prior, while G971b and Gce95 confirm it evaluated as on afterward. I'm also ruling out deploys as the cause, since the deploy logs (T8/T9, T28/T29) show no new releases went out, and all replicas remain on the same revision (T10, T33) — leaving the flag flip as the only change in the window.

So F1 says the flag routes to average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides by this month's purchase count — zero for a shopper who bought before but not this month, matching the ZeroDivisionError at line 47 (G5309). This cause rests entirely on the F1 reading, no S or D row backing it, so cause_rests_on_an_unrun_reading is true but it still reaches a cause.

Now looking at contributing factors, I'm checking whether the 13:43:18 flag revert actually reached the service, since logs show it evaluating as "on" through 13:45 (Gce95) while the provider shows it off starting at 13:43:18.

I want two separate action items here: one to investigate why io-shop kept evaluating monthly-spend-feature as on after the provider switched it off, and another to have the Mitigation Agent verify the service's own flag evaluations show the new value before judging a revert complete.

For the second candidate issue, I'm noting that the code path behind the flag shipped without a test covering a shopper with no purchases this month — F1's proposed tests would fail against the current code, suggesting the fixture doesn't cover that case.

For the third one, the flag was flipped on for all production traffic at once rather than gradually — G971b shows 89 of 200 evaluations on in the first minute, then all 200 from 13:38 per Gce95, with no staged rollout visible.

Nobody got paged on this incident either, and a human on-call might have caught and rolled it back sooner, so I'd link HighErrorRate on io-shop to on-call paging as an action item. AI-1 already addresses CF-2, so now I need to propose finding why io-shop kept evaluating monthly-spend-feature in the first place.

Other items worth capturing: adding a check that flags when the provider's value and the service's own evaluation logs disagree, having the Mitigation Agent confirm actual evaluations before judging a revert successful, rolling out flag changes gradually on io-shop with error-rate monitoring before widening, and routing HighErrorRate alerts to on-call paging.

I'm also weighing whether turning the monthly-spend-feature flag off needs explicit confirmation it reached all of io-shop's replicas before the fix merges, since leaving it on with the unchanged division logic means shoppers with no purchases this month keep failing. I want to phrase these without specific numbers.

For the actual numbers I do need, I'm referencing the line number as a tagged figure rather than writing it directly, calling the source file by its path, and avoiding other digit-containing terms like the PR number or HTTP status code by describing them generically instead ("the draft pull request," "server errors").

Now mapping the event times — flag-on, revert, and reinstatement — plus the log minutes, citing the peak error rate at 13:44 and the evaluation range as tagged references rather than raw figures.

For went_well, Argus quickly tied the ZeroDivisionError to the flag and reverted it shortly after the alert, while Code-Fix drafted a pull request soon after too; putting the flag back when the revert seemed ineffective was questionable since the service never actually saw it go off, so I'll treat that neutrally rather than as clearly good.

For went_wrong, the Mitigation Agent checked the service shortly after the revert but judged it a failure without verifying whether the flag evaluation had actually changed — the logs show the service still evaluating it as on the whole time.

For a second pass, I'm noting a second investigation reached the same conclusion (blaming the already-refuted flag), so Argus escalated without a working fix, and nobody paged anyone which counts as a contributing factor. For got_lucky, I don't see a clear instance to note, so I'll leave it empty. For assumptions, I'm flagging that the F1 mechanism (shoppers who bought before but not this month) wasn't verified, and that the revert's failure to reach the service is inferred from the service's own flag evaluation logs rather than confirmed against the replicas directly.

Now I'm framing the root cause: turning on the monthly-spend feature routes account page requests into average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides this month's total spend by this month's purchase count with no guard against zero, causing a ZeroDivisionError for shoppers with no purchases this month.

For the still-at-risk note, I'm flagging that the feature flag being back on with the unguarded division means failures could recur for shoppers with nothing bought this month, and that a flag-provider switch-off wasn't confirmed to have reached the service. I'm also mapping which evidence IDs support each step of the causal chain, and noting that deploys and replica state were ruled out since revisions were unchanged and healthy before the incident began.

action_items.item: Find out why io-shop kept evaluating monthly-spend-feature as on after it was switched off at the flag provider.
Make io-shop pick up a flag switched off at the provider within a known, short time, and check this by switching off a test flag in production.
Alert when a flag's value at the provider and the value the service logs in its own evaluations disagree.
Have the Mitigation Agent check that the service's own flag evaluations show the new value before it judges a flag revert as having helped or not.
Until the fix is merged, turn monthly-spend-feature off in a way confirmed to reach io-shop's replicas.
Roll out flag changes on io-shop to a small share of traffic first, and watch the account page error rate before widening.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The share of requests answered with server errors rose from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_while_broken} on average, peaking at {errors_at_worst}. The service's own account page error-rate warnings were at their highest at {Gbac1.7}.

From {began}, account page requests failed with ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. Before that minute, the only account page failures logged were shoppers closing the connection, and pages were logged as rendering normally.

ruled_out.what: A deploy. Deploys were read and none came back. The only production change found in the windows read was this flag switch.

The revision the replicas were running. All replicas ran one revision, and the service was measured healthy with it in place before the flag was switched on: errors were at their baseline and account pages were logged as rendering normally.

causal_chain.step: The spend-summary code ran because admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at {P1.1}. Before then the service evaluated the flag as off for every request. In the minute of the switch it evaluated the flag as on for part of its requests, and in each later minute over {Gce95.4} it evaluated it as on for all of them. The ZeroDivisionError failures began in that same minute.

With the flag on, account page requests reach `average_spend_per_item_this_month`. It divides the month's total spend by the number of purchases marked as in the current month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list is empty, and the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1}. The failure reaches the account page. With the flag off, this path is not taken.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary on the account page made those pages fail, likely because the summary divides a shopper's spending this month by the number of things they bought this month, and that sum breaks for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.

contributing_factors.factor: Switching the flag off at the provider did not reach the service. The provider recorded monthly-spend-feature as off from {P2.1}, but the service still logged every evaluation of the flag as on in each minute over {Gce95.4}, and its account page error rate was at its highest at {Gbac1.7}.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Switching the flag off would have taken the failing path out of account page requests from {P2.1}, and the failures would likely have stopped there instead of continuing past the end of the record.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: In the files Code-Fix read, no test ran the monthly summary path with a shopper who had bought nothing this month. That kind of shopper already existed as a test fixture, and Code-Fix reads both of its proposed cases as raising ZeroDivisionError against the current code.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test like that would likely have failed before the flag was ever switched on, and the division would have been found before it reached shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The flag reached all of the service's traffic at once. From the minute after it was switched on, every evaluation the service logged was on. No staged rollout to a small share of traffic was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A small share of account page requests would have failed while the error rate was watched, rather than every request the flag reached.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: No person was paged. No on-call incident was linked to the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have known about the failures when the alert fired. They could have stepped in once the flag revert did not help, rather than the incident going on until it was escalated with a draft fix.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

went_well: The Investigator tied the failures to the flag switch, matching the ZeroDivisionError lines to the minute the flag went on. Argus reverted the flag {T19.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
The revert was made so it could be undone, and it was undone when it did not help.
Code-Fix opened a draft pull request for a person to review {T39.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised. It holds a proposed fix and two tests that run the path the flag enables.
went_wrong: The Mitigation Agent took its first look {T21.1 - T19.1} after the revert. It then judged the revert refuted, and nothing in the record shows it checked whether the service now evaluated the flag as off. The service's logs show it still evaluating the flag as on, so the refutation was of a revert that had not taken effect.
Because the revert was judged refuted, the flag was put back on at {T22.1}.
The second investigation came back with the same flag as the cause. That candidate counted as already refuted, so Argus escalated without a working mitigation in place.

input.root_cause: Switching monthly-spend-feature on sent account page requests into `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's total spend by the number of purchases marked as in the current month and does not check whether that number is zero. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month the count is zero, so line {F1.1} raises ZeroDivisionError, and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: monthly-spend-feature had been switched back on and the division was still unguarded, so account page requests from shoppers with nothing bought this month could keep failing. Switching the flag off at the provider had not been seen to reach the service.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
